description:
The adopter-facing statements of what a fresh repository's rule set contains describe the rules it now receives, and say where the two that left come from.

## Background

Two adopter-facing pages describe the scaffolded rule set and name both opinionated rules as part of it. Once those rules are contributed by a package rather than seeded by the engine, both statements are false for any repository that applied no package — which, after this container, is every repository that did not ask for the workflow.

The correction is small and has to say two things: which rules a bare repository receives, and that the two that left arrive with the workflow package. Without the second, an adopter reads the removal as a regression.

One page is deliberately not touched. The rules-and-gates reference is a projection of this repository's own registry, which keeps declaring both rules for as long as the workflow package contributes them, so it will keep showing them correctly and hand-editing it would be a projection defect.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Neither adopter page presents the two opinionated rules as part of what initialization scaffolds.
- [hard] REQ-02: Both state what a bare repository's rule set contains, and where the two that left arrive from.
- [hard] REQ-03: The fact has one home; the second page cites the first rather than restating it.
- [hard] REQ-04: The projected rules-and-gates reference is unedited, and still renders this repository's own registry.
- [hard] REQ-05: The mechanical documentation checks pass over the changed pages.

## Notes

This states the surface as it is; a narrative of what it used to contain belongs in the release notes.
title: Say which rules a repository is actually scaffolded with
